issues.legal_issue: A co-heir’s possession defeats another co-heir’s partition and possession claim only when it establishes sustained possession to the other’s exclusion under a hostile claim of title.
material_facts: The claimant and the possessor were co-widows entitled to shares in their deceased husband’s property.
The possessor remained in possession of the property after her husband’s death, but continued paying maintenance to the claimant from the property until 1958.
The possessor sought mutation of her name as an heir and insured some of the properties; the court found no evidence that these acts asserted an absolute title excluding the claimant.
There was no evidence that the possessor asserted hostile, exclusive possession for the limitation period before the partition suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The possessor did not establish adverse possession, so the partition and possession suit was not barred by limitation; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A co-heir relying on adverse possession must establish possession to the exclusion of the other co-heir and a hostile claim of title for the required limitation period. Applying that principle, seeking mutation as an heir did not show an exclusive claim, insuring property was an act of management rather than proof of ouster, and paying maintenance from the property did not establish exclusion. The judgment cites no statutory provisions or earlier cases.

predicates.partition_possession_claim_between_cohei: A person claiming a share in property seeks partition and possession against another person who also claims through the same predecessor.
predicates.no_sustained_hostile_exclusion: The possessor did not establish sustained possession excluding the claimant under a hostile claim of title.

issues.definition: When a partition and possession claim is between co-heirs and sustained hostile exclusion is not established, adverse possession is not established.
